frames.ack_checked.note: Any 6 bytes other than the exact ACK frame, a NACK included, give false, and every command returns false in turn. A NACK is not told apart from a garbled frame, and the command is not resent.

frames.checksums_checked.note: LCS is checked before the copy and DCS after it; both failures return 0. The DCS test sums 00 FF LEN LCS as well, which adds 0xFF mod 256, and compares with ~DCS. That is equivalent to the manual's rule.

frames.extended_frames.searched: The FF FF length marker, LENM and LENL, a 16-bit frame length in WriteCommand and ReadData, in src/PN532.cpp and in the local copy PassportPN532.cpp: none.
frames.extended_frames.note: Both directions use one length byte. An extended response has LEN FF and LCS FF, which fails the length checksum test. The packet buffer is 80 bytes in src and 255 bytes in the example copy PassportPN532.

frames.error_frame.searched: TFI 0x7F, the frame 00 00 FF 01 FF 7F 81 00, 'syntax error', 'error frame' in src/ and the driver code of the examples. Every 0x7F hit is crypto or DER code.
frames.error_frame.note: The frame is not recognized as such. It passes the length checksum and is then rejected like any other frame whose TFI is not D5, so the caller gets the same 0 as for any bad frame.

frames.response_code_checked.note: ReadData checks TFI D5 for every response, and each command in src compares byte 1 with its own code + 1.

waiting.irq.searched: IRQ, irq, attachInterrupt, PN532_IRQ, an IRQ pin parameter in the Init functions, ReadPin on anything but MISO, in src/ and all examples.
waiting.irq.note: SAMConfiguration turns on the chip's IRQ output with 0x01, but no Init function takes an IRQ pin and the host never reads one. Waiting is by polling only.

waiting.ready_polling.note: ReadPacket polls the status byte before every read, on SPI and on I2C, in steps of 10 ms.

waiting.bounded_waits.note: WaitReady is the only wait for the chip, and it ends after PN532_TIMEOUT (1000 ms in src, 15000 ms in PassportPN532). The counter adds only the 10 ms sleeps, so the real limit is somewhat longer. The endless block in a repeated begin() is a mutex, not a wait for the chip; it is listed under defects and also reaches the recovery path after a dead chip.

waiting.nonblocking_detect.searched: Use of PN532_COMMAND_INAUTOPOLL (defined, never used), a public pair that starts InListPassiveTarget and collects it later, and calls of IsReady, WaitReady or ReadData from outside the classes, in src/ and all examples.
waiting.nonblocking_detect.note: ReadPassiveTargetID, readIso14443A and readFelica all block in WaitReady for up to PN532_TIMEOUT. IsReady, SendCommandCheckAck and ReadData are protected, so a subclass could split the steps, but neither the library nor an example does.

In the default hardware SPI build on ESP32 the second begin() blocks in SPI.beginTransaction (see defects), so recovery works only with software SPI or I2C. Found by reading the library and arduino-esp32 sources, not run on a board.

several.several_readers.note: The state test passes: PN532.cpp and PN532.h hold no static or global, and all reader state is in the object. Two readers work only with software SPI, though. code_health.errors_returned.note: Failures reach the caller as false, and ReadPassiveTargetID separates no card from failure. All failures in src give the same false, though: the PN532 status code is printed to Serial and dropped, so a timeout, a NACK and an authentication failure look the same. begin() returns void. Only the example class Desfire keeps the code.

code_health.buffers_bounded.note: ReadData checks LEN against the requested size before it copies, and the UID, ATS and rx copies are limited. ReadPassiveTargetID and readIso14443A do not compare the UID length with the frame length, so a short frame could read stale bytes from the packet buffer, but no copy goes out of bounds.

code_health.tests.searched: Test directories and files, unit test frameworks, tests of frame building or parsing: none.

code_health.examples.note: Ten sketches, all on hardware SPI. They also hold code that src lacks: page write, NDEF, DESFire and the larger PassportPN532 copy.

code_health.docs.note: The README covers installation, a minimal sketch and one wiring table; function comments in PN532.cpp add API text. It claims UART support the code lacks, and lists Uno and Mega although library.properties says esp32 only.

code_health.license.note: LICENSE.txt is MIT, but the header of src/PN532.cpp says BSD and the DESFire example code says LGPL, so one file does not cover all the code alike.

defects.what: PN532::begin() on hardware SPI calls SPI.beginTransaction() every time and the library never calls SPI.endTransaction(), so on arduino-esp32 (sources of 2.0.17 and 3.3.12 read, not run on a board), where beginTransaction takes a non-recursive mutex with portMAX_DELAY that only endTransaction releases, a second begin() blocks forever, which hangs the reset path of the DoorOpener sketch, a second reader, and any other SPI library on the bus.
defects.judged: Hardware SPI is the library default and begin() calls SPI.beginTransaction every time with no endTransaction anywhere in src/. In arduino-esp32 2.0.17 and 3.3.12 (libraries/SPI/src/SPI.cpp, read under ~/.platformio/packages/framework-arduinoespressif32 and ~/.cache/Espressif/ComponentManager because ~/.espressif and ~/.arduino15 hold no copy) that call takes a plain mutex with portMAX_DELAY which only endTransaction gives, and HAL locks are on by default, so the sketch's RESET command, a second reader or another SPI library blocks forever with a working chip; read only, not run.

defects.what: ReadPassiveTargetID reads only 28 bytes, so with the preamble present a response above 22 data bytes fails, and a card with an ATS over 7 bytes (7-byte UID) or over 10 bytes (4-byte UID) is reported as a communication failure, which the DoorOpener sketch answers with a chip reset.

dataExchange and communicateThru read rxMax + 8 bytes, one short of the n + 9 bytes a frame with preamble needs (1 + 2 + 2 + 3 + n + 1), so a response that fills the caller's buffer exactly is rejected as too long; the example rx sizes checked leave spare room, so they do not show it.

dataExchange and communicateThru send the command first and then pass rxMax + 8 to ReadData, which returns 0 for anything over PN532_PACKBUFFSIZE, so in src a caller with an rx size above 72 always gets false, after the card has received the command and without the response being collected.
After WaitReady times out the driver returns false without sending the ACK abort frame (no code sends one), so a command still running in the chip is left running when the next command is written.

ReadPassiveTargetID tests uid[0] == 0x80 for a random-ID DESFire, but ISO/IEC 14443-3 (cited from memory, not among the audit sources) marks a random single-size UID with uid0 = 0x08, so CARD_DesRandom is not set for such a card and the sketch's random-ID branch is not reached.
ReadPassiveTargetID returns true with length 0 for a card with a 10-byte UID, which is the same result as no card, so a present card is reported as absent.
The PN532 constructor sets the pin members but not mu8_DebugLevel, which begin() and every command read, so a reader object that is not in static storage starts with an indeterminate debug level.
InitI2C and InitSoftwareSPI call SetPinMode on the reset pin without the 0xFF test that InitHardwareSPI and begin() apply, so 'no reset pin' reaches pinMode as pin 255.

InitHardwareSPI and InitSoftwareSPI set the chip select pin to output but do not drive it high, so until its first transfer the level is whatever the pin holds, and a second reader on a bus is not deselected during the first reader's first transfers.
On I2C the result of Wire.endTransmission() is dropped and WriteCommand returns void, so a write the chip did not acknowledge is seen only as a ready timeout about a second later.
readFelica ignores the result of SwitchOffRfField() and goes on to poll.

In the example copy PassportPN532, with the packet buffer raised to 255, the byte counter in WriteCommand's checksum loop cannot reach P when P is 256 or more, so a txLen of 248 to 253, which dataExchange accepts, loops forever; the inspectors send no command that long.

transports.i2c.note: The I2C path exists but is compiled out: USE_HARDWARE_I2C is FALSE in src/Utils.h with no #ifndef, so a sketch cannot select it without editing the library header. Met: 7-bit address 0x24, status byte first in each read, STOP after each NOT READY poll (Wire.requestFrom ends with STOP). Not met: IsReady() also sends STOP after a READY status and ReadPacket() starts a new read, and a frame longer than the fixed read length is cut by STOP; 6.2.4 says the frame shall be read before STOP. Clock is whatever Wire.begin() sets; the code sets none. Judged by reading; not built or run.

defects.what: Every begin() in the default hardware SPI mode calls SPI.beginTransaction() and nothing calls endTransaction(), and on arduino-esp32 beginTransaction takes a non-recursive mutex with portMAX_DELAY, so a second begin() blocks forever: the DoorOpener re-init path, a second reader, and any other SPI transaction user on the bus (source read: arduino-esp32 3.3.12 and 2.0.16 libraries/SPI/src/SPI.cpp, CONFIG_DISABLE_HAL_LOCKS default n, ESP-IDF components/freertos/FreeRTOS-Kernel/queue.c xQueueSemaphoreTake; not run).
defects.judged: SpiClass::Begin calls beginTransaction and nothing in lib_c calls endTransaction. arduino-esp32 2.0.16 and 3.3.12 SPI.cpp take the plain mutex paramLock with portMAX_DELAY in beginTransaction and give it only in endTransaction, CONFIG_DISABLE_HAL_LOCKS is off in the 2.0.16 sdkconfig, so a second begin(), which the DoorOpener RESET command also reaches on a working chip, or any other transaction user on the bus blocks forever (read, not run).

defects.what: begin() and SamConfig() leave MxRtyPassiveActivation at 0xFF, so with no card ReadPassiveTargetID(), readIso14443A() and readFelica() end in a WaitReady() timeout and return false instead of the documented true with length 0, and no ACK frame is sent, so the chip keeps polling with the RF field on until the next command.
defects.judged: begin() and SamConfig() send no RFConfiguration item 5, so with the default MxRty of 0xFF (7.3.1) and no card the read ends in the 1 s WaitReady timeout and returns false, and nothing aborts the command. A program that calls the public SetPassiveActivationRetries(), as every polling example does, gets the documented result; the README basic sequence omits it.

defects.what: dataExchange() and communicateThru() read rxMax + 8 bytes, but a frame with preamble that carries rxMax data bytes needs rxMax + 9 through DCS, so a response that exactly fills rx fails with 'Packet is longer than requested length' and the clamp to rxMax can never act.

In src/ dataExchange() and communicateThru() with rxMax above 72 always return false, because rxMax + 8 exceeds PN532_PACKBUFFSIZE or wraps in the byte parameter, and ReadData() rejects it after the command has already been sent to the card, so a write may have happened and the response stays unread in the chip.
defects.judged: rxMax + 8 goes through a byte parameter, and ReadData rejects anything above 80 (or below 5 after the wrap) after SendCommandCheckAck has already sent the command, so rxMax above 72 always returns false with the response unread. The function works up to 72 and fails cleanly above it, and the callers in src stay below that, so this is a limit of a legal input.

defects.what: ReadPassiveTargetID() reads a fixed 28 bytes, so an ISO14443-4 card whose ATS is longer than 7 bytes with a 7-byte UID, or 10 bytes with a 4-byte UID, makes it return false as a chip error, which in the DoorOpener example leads to InitReader() and the begin() hang.
ReadPassiveTargetID() reports a card with a 10-byte UID, which 7.3.5 allows as cascade level 3, as true with length 0, the same result as no card.

In I2C mode IsReady() ends each status read with STOP also when RDY = 1 and ReadPacket() then starts a new read, against the 6.2.4 text that the frame shall be read before STOP or its bytes are lost; Fig 31 draws status and frame as separate reads and no hardware test was made, so the loss itself is not shown.

Classic::AuthenticateDataBlock() in the example classes documents 4 or 7 byte UIDs but appends all of them, while 7.3.8 limits authentication data to 10 bytes (Data 0..9), so a 7-byte UID sends a command the chip rejects as a syntax error.

In the passport driver copy (both ICAO examples) the checksum loop in WriteCommand() has a byte counter and P reaches 256 or more with cmdlen of 250 or more, which the 255-byte buffer check allows, so dataExchange() with 248 or more bytes of tx never returns, and cmdlen 255 also wraps LEN to 0.
defects.judged: The counter i is a byte and P is 6 + cmdlen, so with cmdlen of 250 or more i < P is always true and the checksum loop never ends; dataExchange admits that with txLen of 248 to 253. It needs a tx length at the top of what the buffer check allows.

defects.what: In I2C mode the results of Wire.endTransmission() and Wire.requestFrom() are discarded, so a command the chip did not acknowledge at address level, which 6.2.4 says can follow an exchange, is not resent and appears only as a generic ACK timeout.
The constructor does not initialize mu8_DebugLevel, so a PN532 object that is not static prints debug output depending on stack or heap contents.

InitHardwareSPI() and InitSoftwareSPI() set CS as output without driving it high, and arduino-esp32 pinMode() does not set a level, so CS keeps the output latch value until the first transfer, and if that value is low the reader is selected during traffic for another device on a shared bus.
InitI2C() and InitSoftwareSPI() call pinMode on the reset pin with no test for 0xFF, the value begin() and InitHardwareSPI() treat as no pin, which on ESP32 only logs an error.
readFelica() ignores the result of SwitchOffRfField().
README.md claims High Speed UART support, but the code has only SPI, software SPI and I2C.
README.md lists Arduino Uno and Mega, while library.properties declares only esp32.

README.md lists DESFire, DES authentication, NDEF and Reader Test Utilities as library features or examples, but src/ has no such code and no reader test example exists; DESFire and NDEF exist only inside example sketches.
A comment in src/Utils.h says software SPI is the only valid option for the DoorOpener sketch, while the default is hardware SPI and that sketch calls InitHardwareSPI().
The header comment of the passport driver copy says it keeps the original timeouts and receive delays, but PN532_TIMEOUT is 15000 against 1000 and the per-byte SPI receive delay is removed.
